title: A Redocly Alternative for Product Guides, API Docs, and Changelogs
summary: Compare Theneo and Redocly for collaborative product guides, API docs, automated changelogs, private customer portals, and pricing.
body_markdown:
If you’re looking for a Redocly alternative because more people need to maintain your docs, start with your last product release. Who updated the getting-started guide? Did the SDK tutorial still show the old request? How did customers with working integrations find out they needed to change something?


**Theneo is a strong fit when engineers, writers, and product managers share those jobs.** They can edit the same guide, maintain instructions used across several projects, and notify subscribers when a published API change affects them. Redocly is a strong fit when the team’s priority is managing an API description in Git, reviewing pull requests, and testing whether the running API behaves as documented.


## Theneo vs Redocly: what happens when an API field becomes required?


Suppose your payments API is making` merchant_id` mandatory for every new payment. Publishing the updated reference tells a developer the field is required. Getting their first request to work takes one more piece of information: where do they find their merchant ID? Existing customers have another question: when do they need to update their integration?


### Update the API reference and getting-started guide together


In Theneo, import the revised specification and choose how much help you want. If the existing descriptions are good, select the option that fills gaps while preserving them. A writer can update the onboarding guide in the visual editor while an engineer checks the dashboard instructions and request example in the same document. They can resolve questions inline before publishing. Teams that prefer files can also maintain guides as Markdown through Git and the CLI.[See how guides and tutorials work in Theneo.](https://docs.theneo.io/get-started/guides-and-content)


Redocly also supports narrative guides and browser editing. Its Markdown, Markdoc, and React framework gives engineering teams considerable control over the portal, including a rendered preview for each pull request. The choice is where your team prefers to make a change: together on the page in Theneo, or through the repository and review workflow in Redocly.


### Reuse onboarding instructions across guides and partner projects


The directions for finding a merchant ID might appear in your first-payment tutorial, SDK setup guide, and partner onboarding docs. In Theneo, put those directions in a reusable block and embed it in each project. When the dashboard menu moves, a writer edits the shared instruction once. Each guide retains the examples and context its audience needs.[Explore cross-project reusable content.](https://docs.theneo.io/the-editor/content-widgets/reusable-content)


Redocly supports shared content too, including files pulled from other repositories. That model suits teams whose source material belongs to separate engineering groups. Theneo gives the person maintaining the instruction a way to change it directly in the editor across projects.


### Generate release notes and email subscribers about breaking changes


A developer who integrated six months ago may never revisit the quickstart. When you publish the revised spec in Theneo, it compares the new version with the previous one. An optional field becoming required is a change it can flag. Theneo generates a release summary and can email people who subscribed to the changelog. Documentation edits can appear alongside API changes in the release history.[See how automated API changelogs work.](https://www.theneo.io/api-changelog)


The team still supplies the context only it knows. For this release, that means the enforcement date, where existing merchants can find their ID, and which requests they need to update. What Theneo gives you is a route from a published change to the inbox of someone who depends on it. Automated changelogs are included on Starter.


## Which Redocly alternative fits your documentation workflow?


### Starting with Postman, existing guides, or an incomplete API spec


Theneo accepts Postman and Insomnia collections as well as OpenAPI descriptions. You can bring in the reference, add a product walkthrough, and use AI to fill missing field descriptions. Its editor agent can also draft a getting-started section for an author to review. This is useful when your best material is spread across a collection, a guide, and the people who help customers integrate.[Check supported import formats.](https://docs.theneo.io/api-reference/supported-formats)


### Publishing private documentation for partners and customers


On Theneo Enterprise, an administrator invites an external customer by email and assigns the projects they can see. The customer signs in on your branded domain. Section-level controls let you refine access further. For a payments platform, that means a partner can receive its integration guide and enabled API references through one login. Redocly also offers protected documentation and role-based access. Evaluate the actual invitation, assignment, and sign-in experience for the partners you support.[See the private customer portal workflow.](https://docs.theneo.io/your-docs-site/private-customer-portal)


### Choosing AI authoring tools or API governance


Both products support AI and MCP. In Theneo, an authorized client such as Claude or Cursor can search, read, and edit sections in a documentation project. A writer can ask for an update to a guide and inspect the result. Redocly offers an assistant for readers, pull-request review, and an Enterprise early-access Writer agent that proposes fixes through GitHub.[See what an agent can do inside Theneo.](https://docs.theneo.io/ai/ai-in-theneo/theneo-mcp-server)


Redocly has the strong case when engineers need to enforce specification rules in CI, score an OpenAPI description for agent readiness, or run multi-step Arazzo tests against a live API. For a documentation owner whose priority is explaining a change across guides and reaching affected customers, Theneo’s editor and publishing workflow solve the more immediate problem.


## Theneo vs Redocly pricing for hosted documentation


**Theneo Starter is free** and includes one public project, up to two private projects, and up to 20 team members. Business is $120 per workspace per month on annual billing and includes a custom domain, one developer portal, and up to 50 team members. Its seven projects break down into two public and five private, an important distinction if you plan to run several public sites.[View Theneo plans.](https://www.theneo.io/pricing)


**Redocly Pro is $249 per month on annual billing** and includes three projects and unlimited seats. Redocly also has a free open-source renderer for teams that want to host their own API reference. A small team evaluating a hosted workspace has a lower entry point with Theneo; a large contributor group should factor Redocly’s unlimited seats into the comparison. Pricing reviewed November 25, 2026.


## How to evaluate a Redocly alternative before migrating


Start with one real guide and two consecutive versions of an API description. Import the first version into a new Theneo project, add the guide, and subscribe to the changelog. Have a writer and an engineer update a shared instruction, then publish the revised spec. Inspect the reference, the reuse of that instruction, and the email a subscriber receives.


For an existing Redocly portal, include a page with custom Markdoc or React components in the trial. Check images, routes, navigation, and private content before estimating migration effort. For partner documentation, test with two customer accounts that should see different projects.


If your team can take one release from the engineer’s change through the writer’s guide to the customer’s inbox, you’ve tested the part of Theneo that matters most.[Try the Theneo quickstart with your own documentation.](https://docs.theneo.io/get-started/quickstart)
